Situation1: There is a scheduled family gathering on the calendar.
Expectation2: Respect the mentor's time and availability.
Situation2: The mentor fit the session into the last hour before boarding a long flight.
Story: I stared at my phone, the calendar app open, the family gathering circled in bright red. My daughter had called earlier, reminding me how much the grandkids were looking forward to our board game night. I could already picture their eager faces, the laughter, the warmth of being together. But then, just as I was about to leave, my mentor messaged—he had a last-minute window before his flight, the only chance for weeks. He’d squeezed me in, expecting me to make the most of his precious time. I felt the weight of both worlds pressing in: the pull of my family, who counted on my presence, and the responsibility to honor my mentor’s rare availability. My heart raced as I imagined disappointing either side. I wanted to be the reliable grandparent, the one who never missed a moment, but I also wanted to prove myself as a dedicated mentee. The clock ticked, and I stood frozen, torn between two promises, wishing I could be in both places at once.
